title: CLO X PANTONE Master Guest Special Live Replay
description:
CLO and Pantone join forces, the 3D X Color themed live broadcast is finally here!!!!!!  
While enjoying this live broadcast, don’t forget our CLO Year-End Gala on December 30th~~~  
Check our space updates to get the details of the Year-End Gala~~
transcript:
Hello everyone, let's start today's live broadcast.  
Today, we are very honored to invite our little partner, Svea, to participate in our live broadcast.  
Today, Svea will share with you a new digital color design platform called Pantone Connect.  
Next, we will give Svea some time to share with you about the Pantone Connect platform.  

Hello everyone, I am Svea from Pantone.  
Today, I am very happy to receive the invitation from Cloud to share the color inspiration application with everyone.  

In 2020, there was a major event that surprised and panicked everyone.  
It was the spread of COVID-19.  
This event has actually had a great impact on our traditional design process.  
Companies no longer require employees to work at the company as usual.  
Everyone can choose to work remotely.  

In fact, this way of working has caused many difficulties for our designers.  
Because we cannot communicate face-to-face,  
we can only send electronic documents to others for evaluation and feedback.  
And color is one of the design elements most affected by this change.  

Remote work means that team members cannot be in the same environment  
to select colors and communicate with each other.  
Remote work also brings different environmental lighting,  
different computer equipment,  
and so on.  
This greatly increases the difficulty of our color processing workflow.  

Many companies, such as Microsoft, Apple, Facebook, and others,  
have announced that their employees will work from home for a long period.  
Remote work has also become the working method for most people.  
We believe this change is not temporary,  
but will become the new normal for most workers.  

As shown in this picture,  
the living room or study at home will become the new office for our designers.  
Everyone can work freely outside the traditional office.  
This also means that our new office environment may not be ideal for color processing.  

Because designers working at home and in the office have big differences,  
including differences in lighting conditions,  
and the lack of professional design tools.  
Also, the computer displays used by each designer  
may be different.  

So we have to admit that  
designing with color has become a big challenge.  

Next, let’s take a look at the color process.  
What difficulties will we encounter in the color workflow?  

On the left side of the workflow,  
we see that brands and designers focus on  
transforming the color ideas in their customers’ minds  
into defined, applicable color specifications,  
and displaying them in design documents.  
Their goal is to choose the right color,  
apply it consistently in design documents,  
shorten product launch time,  
and reduce overall costs.  

On the right side of the workflow,  
printers and manufacturers need to pre-produce  
and finalize the samples provided to the designers.  
Their goal is to produce the colors in the design documents  
accurately and quickly.  

But in most cases,  
during the color transfer process,  
we print out these design works,  
but because the printed colors are incorrect  
or the colors cannot be realized,  
it causes mismatches between the product colors produced by the manufacturer  
and the colors desired by the designer.  

In this process,  
additional costs, approval procedures, and time losses  
are borne by our companies.  

Because of these reasons,  
we are very happy to launch a product with you,  
our Pantone Connect.  

It is an integrated set of  
physical, digital, and internet-based color workflows.  
This application helps our brand and designer friends  
simplify the color workflow,  
and makes communication easier and more convenient  
when dealing with colors in long-term work.  

No matter where you are,  
at home or in a meeting,  
you can use Pantone Connect  
for color communication.  

We provide software

It can be easily used by designers, brands,  
on mobile phones, computers, tablets,  
and Adobe software.  
You can easily use our application.  

As long as you log in with the same registered account,  
you can access all of our client accounts  
with the same color solutions.  

We see that a good design  
starts with accurate screen colors.  

Why do we need to calibrate screen colors?  
Everyone knows that different displays  
show different colors.  
In such cases,  
it is difficult to judge  
which display shows the most accurate colors.  

Especially in teamwork,  
each person may use a different display,  
or the display models may vary.  
So the colors we see on the screen  
may be slightly different.  

Also, because the screen colors are not accurate,  
the printed colors may be biased as well.  

Therefore, before starting design,  
we need to calibrate the screen colors.  

We can use measurement software like iWall Studio  
to establish a link between the display and the printer.  
We can use iWall Studio  
to quickly measure multiple devices,  
including our display, printer, scanner,  
and projector screen colors.  

In addition, Pantone Connect  
will soon integrate with  
our iWall Studio measurement products.  
It will provide a one-stop solution for color calibration  
and configuration.  

Also, a good workflow  
requires some simultaneous color management tools to assist us.  

For example,  
in terms of inspiration and selection,

like the one on the screen  
to capture colors we like from daily life.  

Then, we can use Pantone Connect  
to check the color accuracy.  
It will provide the Pantone color number.  

Finally, we can use Adobe software  
to design our work  
and provide designers  
with inspiration  
and creative design solutions

Pantone Connect  
is now available free of charge to all our designer friends.

we can extract colors we like

chunks.content: ## Introduction to Pantone Connect and Remote Work Challenges in Color Design This section introduces Pantone Connect, a digital color design platform, and discusses how the COVID-19 pandemic and remote work have transformed traditional color workflows. Key topics include remote work challenges affecting color accuracy and communication, and the growing need for digital color collaboration tools. In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic significantly disrupted traditional design workflows by shifting most employees to remote work. This change impacted color communication and processing, as designers could no longer collaborate face-to-face. Remote environments vary widely in lighting conditions and hardware setups, complicating consistent color selection and evaluation. Companies like Microsoft, Apple, and Facebook have adopted long-term remote work policies, signaling that this shift is likely permanent. Designers working from home often lack professional tools and standardized environments, which makes color accuracy and communication more difficult. The traditional color workflow involves two main parties: - **Brands and Designers:** Focus on translating customers' color ideas into precise, applicable color specifications for design documents, aiming to select accurate colors, maintain consistency, reduce product launch time, and lower costs. - **Printers and Manufacturers:** Need to pre-produce and finalize samples that match design colors quickly and accurately. Color mismatches during printing and production cause delays, additional costs, and extended approval cycles. This highlights the need for improved color workflows and communication. ## Pantone Connect: Overview and Features This section covers the Pantone Connect platform, its integration with various devices and software, essential tools for color accuracy, and how it supports remote collaboration in color workflows. Pantone Connect is an integrated physical, digital, and internet-based color workflow solution designed to simplify color communication and management across different environments. It supports designers, brands, and teams working remotely or in meetings, enabling consistent color usage regardless of location. ### Platform Compatibility - Available on mobile phones, tablets, computers, and Adobe software. - Accessible via a single registered account across devices. - Soon to integrate with iWall Studio measurement products for one-stop color calibration. ### Importance of Screen Color Calibration - Different displays show colors differently, complicating accurate color judgment. - Calibration ensures screen colors are accurate to minimize discrepancies between digital designs and printed outputs. - Tools like iWall Studio measure displays, printers, scanners, and projectors to establish color consistency. ### Color Inspiration and Selection - Users can capture colors from daily life using color comparison cards and photos. - Pantone Connect provides the corresponding Pantone color numbers. - Popular colors from major fashion weeks (e.g., London and New York Fashion Week 2021) are available for trend reference and prediction. ### Color Search and Conversion - Access to tens of thousands of Pantone colors, including solid colors and fabric-specific palettes like TPG and TCX. - Converts between color formats such as RGB, CMYK, LAB, and Pantone-to-Pantone. - Colors can be saved to palettes and shared with team members or partners. - Shared palettes are accessible when collaborators log into their Pantone Connect accounts.

Key topics include remote work challenges affecting color accuracy and communication, and the growing need for digital color collaboration tools. In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic significantly disrupted traditional design workflows by shifting most employees to remote work. This change impacted color communication and processing, as designers could no longer collaborate face-to-face. Remote environments vary widely in lighting conditions and hardware setups, complicating consistent color selection and evaluation. Companies like Microsoft, Apple, and Facebook have adopted long-term remote work policies, signaling that this shift is likely permanent. Designers working from home often lack professional tools and standardized environments, which makes color accuracy and communication more difficult. The traditional color workflow involves two main parties: - **Brands and Designers:** Focus on translating customers' color ideas into precise, applicable color specifications for design documents, aiming to select accurate colors, maintain consistency, reduce product launch time, and lower costs. - **Printers and Manufacturers:** Need to pre-produce and finalize samples that match design colors quickly and accurately. Color mismatches during printing and production cause delays, additional costs, and extended approval cycles.
